observations: The one red read in this round is the page-parsed row in WebKit, 1,008 ms against 1,000, inside the three-spec sweep; four repeats of it alone on the same build gave 814, 569, 581 and 547 ms. That row has been the margin all along and it is a node measurement: in round 5 the same row in Firefox was over the bound in 2 of 4 reads at the head and in 4 of 4 at the pre-fix head 94f1caba, so this head is the better of the two on the row that reds. Its verdict belongs to CI's own runners, where the reviewer already requires the Firefox output to pass before approval; on this evidence the WebKit output deserves the same read.

The streamed-turn row's sample counts differ sharply by engine at the same settings - Chromium 39 part-built batches, WebKit 22, Firefox 96 - so the window the row needs is widest in Firefox and narrowest in WebKit. If it ever goes quiet on a faster runner, WebKit is where it will happen first, and the knob to raise is DISPATCH_STREAM_PROBE_PARAGRAPHS.
